# Card 219: task-force declaration proposal (objection window 219-taskforce)

Category: task-force declaration. Proposed by: product manager (ready), Claude seat, ctx-1 of card 219.
Probe reference: .mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl (23:03 UTC; codex 23:03:08, copilot 23:03:13, grok 23:03:14, agy 23:03:17).
Start: card 219 starts under the product owner's one-card gate waiver (D162; .mob/records/219/record-in-progress.json). The waiver covers card 219 only, ends when the card closes, and changes no gate code. Card 219 implements D159 (C1 to C3, per D159 C5).
Order: the waiver lets 219 start despite the open failures; where it sits in the queue is the team's call at the next re-rank boundary (D162 placement).

## Task force
- Product manager (ready): Claude | why: refines card 219 at ready; keeps the Done checks within D157 (three, one criterion each), names the value and metric, and confirms the Intent line (D165) will quote D159 and D162 | context: ctx-1
- Architect (slice): Claude | why: places the change in scripts/mob_process.py (how "previous record" is chosen from record_commits order instead of max(n < card)), numbers the criteria 1 to 3 before red (D157), and checks the change stays within D136; the card record checker requires a slice seat | context: ctx-2
- QA engineer (red): Claude | why: turns each Done check's ZOMBIES into failing tests in tests/test_mob_process.py with fixture repositories (a higher-numbered record committed before a lower-numbered one; genuine and back-dated evidence), one criterion per red-green cycle (D157), writes the "Intent:" line before the first red (D165), red first (D137) | context: ctx-3
- Backend developer [author] (green, refactor): Claude | why: changes the previous-record choice in scripts/mob_process.py so each red test passes, and nothing else in the evidence checks; the author does not review or QA their own increment | context: ctx-4
- Independent reviewer (audit lens) [reviewer]: Claude | why: non-author review of the diff against D159 C1 to C3 and its invariants (every other evidence check unchanged; records already on main stay valid), with a loophole lens: can back-dated evidence pass, can the first record in history have a "previous", does the error name the record compared with | context: ctx-5
- Delivery lead (ship): Claude | why: confirms CI, the card record, the probe lines and that the commits cite D159 and D162 before each commit lands; the card record checker requires a ship seat with its own commit evidence | context: ctx-6
- Product manager (signoff): Claude | why: a fresh context signs off against the three Done checks, because the refinement seat may not hold the second seat | context: ctx-7

Seven seats cover the six roles the card record checker requires (ready, slice, red, green, ship, signoff) plus the independent reviewer. The reviewer seat is named "Independent reviewer (audit lens)", never "auditor": auditor_seated_problems refuses any card seat whose role contains "auditor", because the auditor is external to the mob and never seated.

## Left out
UX designer and frontend developer (no user interface); database developer (no such code); security (no new trust boundary: the checker only reads git history, and the independent reviewer checks that back-dated evidence is still refused); technical writer (no document); language designer and grammar designer (no language change); performance engineer (no hot path: one lookup per record); DevOps / runner expert (the checker is a Python script run by the facilitator, the pre-push hook and CI, but the card changes neither the hook, the workflow nor the runner); agile coach (no process change: D157, D158 and D165 are applied, not changed; the rule change itself was decided by D159).

## Domain expert (refinement)
Should a member with different domain knowledge or context join now? No. The card is a small change to one function's choice of "previous record" in scripts/mob_process.py, with its tests; the architect and backend developer already work in that script (cards 195, 205 and 214 used the same record checker). The risks specific to it (git history order versus card number, back-dated evidence, a record with no earlier record, the error naming the record) are exactly the Done checks and their ZOMBIES, each pinned by a red test in a fixture repository, and the independent reviewer (audit lens) carries the loophole lens above. The one adjacent concern is how git orders commits (`record_commits`); the backend developer and reviewer cover it, and if a slice needs knowledge no seat holds, any member adds an expert through a Decider (mid-card addition, with the Decider id). Adding a seat now would add a context and a poll without a gap it fills.

## Reason for Claude seats
Probes at 23:03 UTC (.mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl) show Codex, Copilot, Grok and agy without usable quota: codex "You've hit your usage limit" (exit 1); copilot has_quota=False remaining=-5 entitlement=1500 (resets 2026-11-01); grok 402 Payment Required, usage balance exhausted; agy 429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (resets in 46h22m). Each seat is a distinct fresh context (ready ctx-1, slice ctx-2, red ctx-3, green ctx-4, reviewer ctx-5, ship ctx-6, signoff ctx-7), and nobody reviews or QAs their own increment. Non-Claude models come first again as soon as a fresh probe shows quota (D163: balanced rotation, not a rule against Claude).

## Product value and metric
Value the card returns to: cards 208 and 209 are finished and signed off, but their schema-1 records are held unpushed (blocker .mob/records/blockers/2026-10-30-209-record-order.md and its 23:3x update) because the record checker compares each card's evidence with the next-lower card number, and card 214 closed first. Today a card that closes out of number order cannot be closed by the checker's rules, and re-ranking (D148) makes out-of-order closes normal; card 213 will hit the same refusal. When this lands, the two held records can land and later out-of-order closes are not refused, while back-dated evidence is still refused.
Metric that moves: (1) held records, the count of finished cards whose record is held back by the checker (today 2: 208 and 209; target 0 once 219 is on main and they land); (2) refused-record events per close, the number of checker refusals of the form "evidence ... predates Card NNN's record" per card close, counting only genuine (not back-dated) evidence (today 2: the refusals of 209 and 208, both recorded in the blocker file; target 0). Companion check, not a target: back-dated evidence refused stays at every attempt (Done check 2). Both are read from the blocker records and from check runs in git, not self-reported by the seats.

## Intent line (D165)
Before the first red of each criterion that implements owner direction, the red seat writes "Intent: <what the owner wants and why>" in its record, quoting the owner and naming the D-number. For this card the direction is D159 (the "previous record" follows record commit order, not card number; back-dated evidence stays refused; the error names the record compared with) and D162 (the product owner's word "waive": card 219 may start despite the open failures; one card only). The facilitator confirms the line against those records (D165 C2); the criterion is "no intent question" only where mechanical.

## D157 applies
One acceptance criterion per red-green cycle, checked from git (5-card experiment, D157):
- The slice (architect, ctx-2) numbers the criteria 1 to 3 before any red.
- Each red commit body carries "Criterion: n".
- The green for criterion n lands before any red for n+1.
- Greens are pushed at once.
- ZOMBIES already in the card are implemented by QA, not rewritten (a ZOMBIES change is a card-text fix through this window).
- Each commit stays within D136, cites D159 (and D162 where it applies), references D145 and D136, red first (D137). Per D145 C2 the checker change cites D159, recorded in an ancestor commit.

## D158 applies
The facilitator's pre-window checklist (D158) is run before this window opens: the proposal names seats for ready, slice, red, green, ship and signoff; the reviewer seat is not named auditor; the roster is not template boilerplate; every seat has a domain/why and a distinct context; the Claude reason cites a probe file and time (23:03 UTC); the card text lines match the proposal (second section below); every declared role is listed for polling (checklist file to be committed before the window, as for windows 208-taskforce and 210-taskforce); the repository (phrase-lang, not mob-defaults) and the working directory of every command are named.

## Window rule
- Every declared role is polled (F-054): all seven role seats answer (ready ctx-1 is the proposer; slice ctx-2, red ctx-3, green ctx-4, reviewer ctx-5, ship ctx-6, signoff ctx-7), each in its own fresh context. A declared role that is not polled makes the window invalid.
- Each seat answers either "no objection" or ONE fixed condition per objection (D145). A condition that is simply adopted and re-polled stays in the window; an unsettled objection goes to a full Decider.
- Card-text changes proposed with this declaration are card-text fixes in the same window (D153 L1).

## Why this is neither a one-way door nor a standing-rule change
Two-way door: the declaration ends with the card (and can be re-declared by another window); nothing is published, deleted or migrated, and the roster can be changed by a Decider mid-card. The checker change the card makes is itself reversible (D159 REVERSIBILITY: revert the checker commit; no records or earlier D-records change). It is not a standing-rule change: the rule change (how "previous record" is chosen) was decided by D159, and the gate waiver by the product owner in D162; this declaration applies Task-Force Driven Development, D136, D145, D153, D157, D158 and D165 as written and changes no agreement, D-record or checker. The waiver is one card only and ends when 219 closes; every other card still follows the corrective-card gate.
